judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain definitional passage assigning labels to the two named entities; no term in it carries two reasonable meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It identifies DSI as 'the lender' consistently with the Description of Services and the arbitration clause's use of 'Lender'; nothing elsewhere contradicts it, though the arbitration section expands 'we/us' to officers and affiliates, a definition that sits beside rather than against this one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligations are phrased as attempts ('we will attempt to', 'where available', 'certain CAB services', 'estimated period ... one day'), so the boundary of what is actually promised for the CAB fee is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its statement that the LOC 'secures your repayment of the loan on its due date' and is not open-ended must be read with the LOC clause's 175-day expiry and the Default clause's right to collect checks; the fit is workable but the services/fee relationship is a plausible source of argument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short sentence characterising the fee as non-interest yet part of the TILA finance charge; nothing vague or double-meaninged in it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the Cost and Payment Terms provision, which likewise splits the Finance Charge into Lender interest and the CAB fee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is riddled with blanks and garbled tokens ('°%', 'ofS', 'Joan'), and the statement that the fee is 'earned in advance at the inception of the loan' sits awkwardly against the promised prorated refund on prepayment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unfilled spaces are directly contradicted by the signature block's certification that the customer received this agreement 'WITH ALL NECESSARY SPACES COMPLETED', and the refund language must be squared with the Notice of Cancellation's return-of-payments promise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fee amounts and triggers are specified numerically, though 'the State Allowed Returned Item Fee, whichever is greater' and the open-ended 'costs of collection' leave some edge uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks the LOC reimbursement obligation and the Collection Expenses clause's attorneys'-fee promise without contradicting either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentences are mechanically corrupt and truncated ('unlgyuful excess', 'maximug peepee law', 'amortiz'), leaving the usury-savings sentence literally unfinished, and 'irrevocable' LOC sits against automatic revocation on cancellation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The truncated savings language duplicates and is completed by the COMPLIANCE clause, and the revocation-on-cancellation sentence must be read with the three-day Notice of Cancellation; those relationships are largely harmonising but the duplication invites argument about which text governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We shall have the right to seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us' is open as to what 'seek collection' permits, and it is followed by the catch-all 'any other right or remedy allowed by law', a general term appended to an enumerated specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This remedy sits directly against the Collection Expenses clause's statement that 'a person may not threaten or pursue criminal charges ... related to a check', and the two together are exactly the pairing a court would have to reconcile in a check-referral dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is a one-sided list of lender prerogatives, and 'we are not required to file suit or arbitrate' is a broad phrase whose reach against the mandatory arbitration section is not defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That phrase pulls against the Arbitration Agreement's 'Upon the election by either you, us, or Lender, any Claim shall be resolved by binding arbitration' and against the no-waiver-by-delay language relied on in waiver arguments, a genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear in its operation, though 'if you do not reject that Arbitration Agreement' uses 'reject' where the arbitration section speaks of 'opt out', a small terminological slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly disclaims modifying the Arbitration Agreement and Limitation on Class Participation, so it harmonises with the No Jury Trial and Opting Out provisions rather than conflicting with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard usury-savings boilerplate with a single OCR slip ('applicable Jaw'); its operation is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substantially duplicates the savings language at the end of the LOC clause, which is harmless overlap rather than inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prior to initiating any claim ... you must provide ... a reasonable opportunity of not less than 60 days to cure' is a condition precedent whose scope ('any claim that this agreement or related matter ... is legally non-compliant') and cure standard are indefinite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the Arbitration Agreement's right to demand arbitration 'at any time' and with the small-claims carve-out in the Claim definition; whether a 60-day notice precedes an arbitration demand is not addressed anywhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bolted-on sentence 'A person may not threaten or pursue criminal charges ... in the absence of forgery, fraud, theft, or other criminal conduct' ends in a general catch-all after specific crimes, and 'threaten or pursue' is itself contestable when applied to a worthless-check affidavit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands against the Default clause's right to 'seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us', and the two provisions read together are what a court would have to harmonise on the check-referral question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single stipulation of fact with no operative ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the FAA choice in the Governing Law clause and contradicts nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, definite sentences; 'at our discretion' is one-sided but not uncertain in meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the arbitration or entire-agreement provisions cuts against it, though the arbitration section's extension of 'we/us' to affiliates touches the same ground without conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely informational addresses and a phone number; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The opt-out clause directs notice to 'PLS Financial Services' at the same Chicago address rather than to PLS Loan Store of Texas named here, a minor entity mismatch across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You and we agree to arbitrate Claims instead of having them decided in court' reads as an unconditional commitment, which is broader than the election-based mechanism that follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Starting an Arbitration clause ('Upon the election by either you, us, or Lender'), the small-claims carve-out and the opt-out right, so the headline and machinery do not perfectly align.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in 'the actions of you, us, Lender, or third parties' and any 'dispute ... arising from or relating to' the agreement, so whether conduct like a referral to a prosecutor is a 'Claim' is genuinely arguable; the carve-outs add a further expressio unius problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth must be squared with the opt-out clause's narrower statement that 'only those disputes ... arising under this Agreement will be excluded from arbitration' and with the Pre-Suit Notice condition, which are not fully aligned with each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Either you, we, or Lender may give written notice ... at any time, even if the other party has begun a lawsuit' is the kind of open-ended election language that invites dispute about how long the right survives, and 'reasonably satisfactory to us' is a one-sided vague standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read against the Notices and Waivers clause ('we are not required to file suit or arbitrate'; 'we may waive or delay enforcing our rights without losing them') and against the Pre-Suit Notice provision, which together complicate when arbitration can still be demanded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mostly definite procedure, but 'such other location as we or Lender may agree' omits the customer, and the direction that the arbitrator 'will apply relevant law' yet not the rules of evidence or procedure is loosely bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the FAA choice in the Governing Law clause and with the severability clause's rule that this agreement controls over the organisation's code.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional entry-of-judgment provision with a definite deeming rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the Arbitration Procedure and Governing Law provisions without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opt-out notice is directed to 'PLS Financial Services' rather than the contracting party PLS Loan Store of Texas, a mechanical misnaming that could matter to whether an opt-out was properly given.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its limitation that 'only those disputes ... arising under this Agreement will be excluded' is narrower than the Claim definition, which reaches prior agreements and third-party conduct, so the two provisions describe different perimeters.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain and explanatory; the omission of Lender from 'neither you nor we will be able to litigate' is a slip of little consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the jury waiver and opt-out mechanics already stated in the Waiver of Right to Trial by Jury and Opting Out clauses without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If either you, we, or Lender ... choose arbitration, all Claims must be arbitrated' is emphatic and detailed; the drafting is one-sided but the meaning of the class waiver is not uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the arbitration organisation-selection rule barring organisations that permit class actions, and with the severability paragraph that follows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability plus an order-of-precedence rule; both operate definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the Entire Agreement clause's reformation-and-severance language, but the two are complementary rather than inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short choice-of-law rule with an express carve-out; the only oddity is the stray quotation mark in 'FAA’)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Arbitration Procedure clause's FAA designation and the Interstate Commerce stipulation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory-style warning rather than an operative term; nothing in it allocates rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'short-term needs only' message coexists with the refinancing language in the Description of Services and Cost Terms, but that is commercial tension, not a contradiction of an operative obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contact information for a regulator; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision bears on it, though the Pre-Suit Notice requirement addresses a different channel and does not purport to limit regulator complaints.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional integration, no-oral-modification and reformation language, all definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'The entire agreement between you and us' sits against a transaction that expressly incorporates a separate Credit Services Disclosure Statement, two Notices of Cancellation and a separate lender loan agreement, so the integration's perimeter is not obvious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is a stack of acknowledgments and warranties, including a certification that the agreement was received 'WITH ALL NECESSARY SPACES COMPLETED' and a warranty of 'no intention to file a petition' in bankruptcy, the latter an inherently uncertain state-of-mind term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The completed-spaces certification is contradicted by the blank Cost and Payment Terms and the blank cancellation deadline in the Notice of Cancellation, a concrete internal mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deadline is measured from 'THE DATE OF THE TRANSACTION', which is not defined anywhere in the agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The attached Notices of Cancellation measure the same right as 'within three days after the date the contract is signed', a different trigger for the identical right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and clear on its face, but 'within three days after the date the contract is signed' differs from the midnight-of-the-third-day formulation used elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts in trigger and expression with the NOTICE of right to cancel on page 4 ('before midnight of the third day after the date of the transaction'), a direct provision-to-provision mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite ten-day refund promise; 'any payment made by you under this contract' is broad but readable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the Cost and Payment Terms statement that the CAB fee is 'earned in advance at the inception of the loan' and with the LOC clause's automatic revocation on timely cancellation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative deadline is left blank ('not later than midnight on'), so the provision as written fixes no date, and the addressee is stated twice in a garbled way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blank leaves the cancellation deadline to be supplied by the two differently worded cancellation provisions on page 4 and above, which do not agree on the trigger date.
